subject: Discovery recap: migrating from OpenAI/Anthropic to open models — technical fit and next steps

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: migrating from OpenAI/Anthropic to open models — technical fit and next steps

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we all have the same set of priorities and next steps. I captured the pain, the current stack, and what success looks like for Fintech Labs. Please flag any corrections.

Key pain points you stated
- Escalating per-token costs on current OpenAI calls affecting margin on high-volume transactions.
- Occasional rate-limit/throughput throttling during peak reconciliation windows (midnight batch runs).
- Data residency/logging constraints for audit (need request-level audit logs for customer-facing flows).

Current stack / usage patterns
- Production: ~9 million tokens/mo across ingestion + user prompts. Primary inference: OpenAI GPT-4 for customer-facing summarization and Anthropic Claude for risk analysis.
- Typical latency budget: 300–700ms p50 for single-turn summaries; background batch jobs can tolerate up to 2s.
- Most calls are synchronous REST from service layer; KV cache not widely used today.

Compatibility & integration requirements
- Must support existing REST call flows and match role-based prompt templates with minimal changes (prefer a drop-in SDK option).
- Prefer continued streaming support for long responses (partial render).
- Model outputs must be stable for A/B parity tests — we need deterministic-ish sampling config and ability to pin model versions.

Shortlist of open models we discussed (initial):
- Llama 2 13B (int8/4-bit quant) — good balance of quality/cost for summarization.
- Mistral Instruct 7B — promising for instruction tuning on risk prompts.
- RedPajama-Instruct 3B/7B — low-cost option for high-throughput non-sensitive scoring.
- Falcon 7B/40B variants — candidate for higher-quality replacement of Anthropic in risk analysis.

Success criteria for a pilot
- Cost reduction goal: reduce total inference cost per token by >=40% while preserving output quality within tolerance.
- Performance: p50 latency <= 700ms for interactive flows at target throughput.
- Security/compliance: ability to store audit logs for 12 months and support an SOC2 review.

Proposed immediate next steps
1) Share a short POC template (attached) — fill in typical payload sizes, concurrency targets, and 2–3 representative prompts.
2) Redwood SE team to size throughput (GPU vCPU mix) and provide rough cost delta vs current usage.
3) Fintech Labs to run a small set of golden prompts for quality checks and provide baseline outputs from OpenAI/Anthropic.
4) Procurement: share any procurement timelines or gating items (PO, security questionnaire).

Attachments: redwood-poc-template.xlsx, security-evidence-summary.pdf, rough-sow-draft.docx

I'll loop Rishi from SE to size the PoC — copying him on a follow-up. If that all looks right, can we target an initial PoC kickoff the week of Mar 23?

Thanks,

Hi Samir — thanks for the clarifying questions. Quick answers and next actions below.

Sizing & cost (ballpark) — for the scenarios you described (9M tokens/mo, mixed interactive + batch):
- Llama 2 13B int8: expected ~35–45% cost reduction vs GPT-4 baseline; single-instance p50 latency ~450–600ms for 1–2 concurrent interactive requests; recommend a 3-node pool with autoscaling for peak windows.
- Mistral Instruct 7B: expected ~50–60% cost reduction for instruction-style tasks; latency ~300–450ms p50; good candidate for risk prompts after fine-tuning.

Engineering notes:
- Streaming: both models supported via Redwood streaming endpoints; you may need small client changes if you currently depend on OpenAI-specific SSE chunk shapes — we provide a compatibility shim in our SDK.
- Tokenization: minor differences expected; recommend running the golden prompts to identify any edge cases.
- Caching: enable prefix KV cache for interactive summaries to reduce token counts by ~10–20% where prompts share prefixes.

Security artifacts
- SOC2 and security packet: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/FintechLabs-POC (attachment security-evidence-summary.pdf). I'll also send a signed SOC2 AOC to procurement under separate secure link.

Next steps
1) Please complete the attached POC template with representative payloads and concurrency targets.
2) We’ll stand up a 2-week single-model PoC (choose Llama 2 13B int8 or Mistral 7B) — Redwood provides reserved capacity during the PoC.
3) Schedule kickoff: I propose Tue Mar 24 10am PT. Monica — can you confirm?

I attached the redwood-poc-template.xlsx and rough-sow-draft.docx for procurement. Happy to jump into a quick call with your infra team if helpful.

Cheers,
